mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rebound for several consecutive weeks, commuting and foot traffic recover first in central shopping areas, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days after simultaneous week-on-week gains in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, or instead remains below the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week increase in RESIDENTIAL, especially when WORKPLACES stays depressed, indicates people are staying home more and making fewer discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises at least 3 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES remains below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or does not fall over the next 14 days after the specified RESIDENTIAL increase while WORKPLACES stays weak.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent recovery in GROCERY_PHARM alongside a smaller improvement in PARKS signals broader local out-of-home activity and neighborhood circulation, which spills into retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its previous 28-day mean despite sustained improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS over the next month.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls below its recent average by more than 5 points for a week, access frictions and suppressed city-center movement reduce shopping trips, causing RETAIL_REC to decline within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after a qualifying TRANSIT drop, or instead increases relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS continues to improve while RETAIL_REC is still deeply negative, warmer-weather leisure substitution draws time away from indoor retail and keeps retail mobility from recovering over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -50
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean despite a two-week PARKS increase while RETAIL_REC stays below -50 at the trigger point.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM combined with weaker RESIDENTIAL growth indicates more essential errand chaining outside the home, which should translate into a modest retail rebound within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL growth slows or falls.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays below -45 for another week after already improving, the labor-market recovery is still too weak to support discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -45 for at least one more week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its prior 28-day mean over the next month despite WORKPLACES staying below -45 for the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous easing in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals that commuting and office visits are restarting together, and this co-movement should lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES trend upward together from the snapshot levels.
